To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the nucleoid-associated protein Fis is required for spatial regulation of Z ring assembly during bacterial cytokinesis; (2) Fis is required to prevent premature Z ring assembly in the midcell region; and (3) Fis binds the Z ring protein FtsA to prevent Z ring assembly in midcell.

a nucleoid-associated protein called SlmA mediates nucleoid occlusion of the bacterial division machinery, and that SlmA is a member of a novel family of proteins that bind to the nucleoid and regulate the cell cycle.
the bacterial nucleoid-associated protein, HU, is a spatial regulator of the bacterial cell division protein FtsZ and that HU is required for the spatial regulation of FtsZ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which bacteria regulate their cell division.
the spatial control of bacterial cell division.
the mechanisms by which bacteria divide and grow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nucleoid occlusion system is a spatial regulatory system that prevents the assembly of the Z ring at the nucleoid.
the protein Z-ring is a protein ring that forms in the middle of a cell, and is involved in cytokinesis.
the nucleoid-associated protein HU mediates nucleoid occlusion of the bacterial Z ring, and this is the first mechanistic understanding of this spatial regulation of cytokinesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new protein, Slm, that is required for the spatial regulation of cytokinetic ring assembly in Bacillus subtilis.
we have identified a new mechanism for spatial regulation of cytokinesis in bacteria, and that this mechanism is mediated by nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs).
we have discovered a protein that is responsible for the nucleoid occlusion phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleoid-associated protein HU is a key regulator of Z-ring assembly in B. subtilis and that this regulation is mediated by the ability of HU to bind DNA.
the nucleoid-associated protein Hda (helicase-activating protein) mediates nucleoid occlusion of FtsZ polymerization.
the nucleoid is an important spatial regulator of bacterial cytokinesis.
